10.translation: Gratuito, injustificado o sin razón fundada
10.example: Critics objected to the gratuitous depictions of violence in the documentary film.

10.translation: Agravio, queja o motivo de protesta legítima
10.example: Union representatives filed an official grievance regarding unsafe laboratory ventilation.

10.translation: Heterogéneo o compuesto por elementos disímiles
10.example: The urban metropolis boasts a heterogeneous population representing over one hundred cultures.

10.translation: Jerarquía o estructura escalonada de mando
10.example: Primate troops organize social tasks through a dynamic and clearly defined dominance hierarchy.

10.translation: Hipótesis comprobable planteada al inicio de un estudio
10.example: The clinical trials failed to substantiate the initial hypothesis regarding drug efficacy.

10.translation: Perjudicar o mermar una función sensorial o mecánica
10.example: Prolonged exposure to industrial noise above ninety decibels can permanently impair hearing.

10.translation: Imparcial, objetivo y sin sesgos
10.example: Referees must render an impartial judgment regardless of team affiliations.

10.translation: Inequidad, desigualdad o injusticia manifiesta
10.example: Educational reformers mobilized to eliminate socioeconomic inequities in public school funding.

10.translation: Inevitable o seguro que sucederá
10.example: With tectonic pressure mounting along the fault line, a seismic release was deemed inevitable.

10.translation: Inherente o inseparable de la naturaleza de algo
10.example: A degree of uncertainty is inherent in all probabilistic meteorological forecasts.

10.translation: Jurisdicción o ámbito legal de autoridad
10.example: Maritime incidents outside territorial waters fall under international admiralty jurisdiction.

10.translation: Yuxtaposición de elementos para resaltar contrastes
10.example: The photographer's juxtaposition of ancient stone temples and neon skyscrapers highlights urban tension.

10.translation: Parentesco o vínculo fraternal y de afinidad
10.example: Anthropologists documented complex kinship systems that govern clan marriages and inheritance.

10.translation: Lamentar o expresar hondo pesar
10.example: Environmentalists lament the irreversible extinction of flightless bird species on isolated islands.

10.translation: Legítimo, lícito y conforme a la ley y razón
10.example: Independent observers confirmed the referendum was conducted under fully legitimate democratic norms.

10.translation: Magnitud, dimensión o escala de un suceso
10.example: Seismologists estimated the earthquake's oceanic epicenter reached a magnitude of 8.2.

10.translation: Metodología sistemática de investigación académica
10.example: The paper dedicates five chapters to explaining its rigorous double-blind methodology.

10.translation: Monopolio comercial de un mercado
10.example: Antitrust regulators sued the rail conglomerate to dismantle its regional freight monopoly.

10.translation: Despreciable, insignificante o trivial
10.example: The temperature discrepancy was negligible and did not alter the chemical crystallization outcome.

10.translation: Novedoso, original y sin precedentes
10.example: The engineers formulated a novel biodegradable plastic derived from marine brown algae.

10.translation: Nocivo, perjudicial o tóxico para la salud
10.example: Firefighters wore pressurized breathing apparatus to avoid inhaling noxious chemical fumes.

10.translation: Matiz o sutileza sutil de significado
10.example: Poetry translation requires deep sensitivity to nuance, meter, and metaphorical cadence.

10.translation: Inconsciente o ajeno a lo que le rodea
10.example: Absorbed in his headphones, the commuter was completely oblivious to the commotion around him.

10.translation: Omnipotente o que todo lo puede
10.example: Ancient mythologies often depicted sky deities as omnipotent rulers over natural elements.

10.translation: Paradigma o modelo conceptual dominante en una disciplina
10.example: The theory of general relativity triggered a radical paradigm shift in theoretical physics.

10.translation: Paradoja o contradicción aparente
10.example: The Fermi paradox questions why intelligent extraterrestrial civilizations have not contacted Earth.

10.translation: Perpetuar o prolongar la existencia de algo
10.example: Biased textbooks can perpetuate inaccurate historical myths across successive generations.

10.translation: Plausible, verosímil y razonable
10.example: Astrobiologists consider the subsurface oceans of Europa a plausible harbor for microbial life.

10.translation: Situación difícil, penosa o apuro grave
10.example: Humanitarian agencies raised global awareness regarding the desperate plight of drought refugees.

10.translation: Postular un principio como base de un razonamiento
10.example: Quantum cosmologists postulate the existence of multidimensional string vibrations.

10.translation: Propenso o inclinado a sufrir algo negativo
10.example: Low-lying agricultural valleys near rivers are historically prone to seasonal flash floods.

10.translation: Partidario o defensor de una causa o teoría
10.example: Proponents of renewable energy emphasize its long-term cost benefits and zero emissions.

10.translation: Cualitativo o relativo a cualidades y descripciones
10.example: Sociologists complemented statistical tables with in-depth qualitative interview transcripts.

10.translation: Cuantitativo o medible en cifras numéricas
10.example: Economists rely on quantitative macroeconomic indicators like GDP growth and unemployment rates.

10.translation: Cuarentena o aislamiento preventivo de bioseguridad
10.example: Livestock imported from foreign continents was placed in thirty-day veterinary quarantine.

10.translation: Conciliar o hacer compatibles dos posturas
10.example: It is arduous to reconcile corporate profit maximization with aggressive environmental preservation.

10.translation: Repercusión o consecuencia indirecta de un acto
10.example: The unexpected closure of the Suez Canal had cascading repercussions across global supply chains.

10.translation: Requisito indispensable o necesario
10.example: A master's degree in linguistics is a requisite qualification for this research fellowship.

10.translation: Resiliencia o capacidad de sobreponerse a catástrofes
10.example: Mangrove forests demonstrate astonishing ecological resilience following tropical hurricanes.

10.translation: Retener información o conservar una cualidad
10.example: Mnemonic techniques help language learners retain irregular verb patterns over decades.

10.translation: Riguroso, estricto y de máxima exigencia científica
10.example: Pharmaceutical candidates undergo rigorous clinical evaluation across four distinct phases.

10.translation: Examinar minuciosamente con rigor analítico
10.example: Peer reviewers scrutinize every statistical chart before approving manuscripts for publication.

10.translation: Espontáneo o producido sin estímulo externo forzado
10.example: Chemical reactions that release free energy often occur spontaneously under standard conditions.

10.translation: Subordinado o de rango inferior en una escala
10.example: In military structures, junior lieutenants are strictly subordinate to commanding captains.

10.translation: Subsecuente, posterior o que sigue en el tiempo
10.example: The discovery and subsequent commercial rollout of antibiotics revolutionized global healthcare.

10.translation: Subvencionar o financiar con fondos públicos
10.example: Many nations subsidize solar panel installations to accelerate clean power adoption.

10.translation: Fundamentar o validar con pruebas fehacientes
10.example: Historians unearthed archival diaries to substantiate claims about early trade corridors.

10.translation: Sintetizar o combinar elementos diversos en un todo armónico
10.example: In the conclusion, students synthesize insights from sociology, economics and ecology.

10.translation: Tangible, palpable y demostrable con hechos
10.example: The trade agreement delivered tangible economic growth to coastal shipping ports.

10.translation: Tenue, frágil o débilmente sostenido
10.example: The correlation between the two demographic variables proved statistically tenuous upon retesting.

10.translation: Transitorio, fugaz o de corta permanencia
10.example: Seasonal migratory songbirds are transient visitors across the city's botanical parkways.

10.translation: Ubicuo o presente en todas partes de manera generalizada
10.example: Microplastics have become ubiquitous in ocean ecosystems from the equator to the poles.

10.translation: Socavar o minar la autoridad o estabilidad
10.example: Spreading unverified rumors undermines public trust in scientific institutions.

10.translation: Inequívoco, rotundo y sin lugar a dudas
10.example: Laboratory spectroscopy gave unequivocal evidence that the mineral contained extraterrestrial helium.

10.translation: Sin precedentes o jamás registrado antes
10.example: The heatwave shattered centuries-old regional records with unprecedented thermal intensity.

10.translation: Validar o confirmar la exactitud científica
10.example: Repeating experimental trials across three continents validated the cancer screening technique.

10.translation: Venerar o profesar profundo respeto
10.example: Many indigenous societies venerate mountain peaks as sacred ecological sanctuaries.

10.translation: Viable o con capacidad para prosperar y sostenerse
10.example: Urban farming presents an economically viable alternative for reducing food transport emissions.

10.translation: Vulnerable o expuesto a sufrir daño o agresión
10.example: Coastal wetlands are acutely vulnerable to sea level rise caused by polar thermal melting.

10.translation: Cauteloso, receloso o en estado de alerta
10.example: Experienced wildlife trackers are wary of sudden silences in the rainforest canopy.

10.translation: Generalizado o extendido por amplias zonas
10.example: Solar panel installations enjoyed widespread public enthusiasm and government subsidies.

10.translation: Rendimiento, producción o ceder ante la fuerza
10.example: Genetic crop enhancements increased agricultural yield by forty bushels per acre.

10.translation: Flexible o que produce resultados
10.example: The scientist's yielding experiments led to novel breakthroughs in superconducting ceramics.

10.translation: Celo, fervor y apasionamiento por una causa
10.example: The reformist attorney pursued human rights cases with indefatigable missionary zeal.

10.translation: Cenit, apogeo o punto más alto de gloria o el cielo
10.example: The Roman Empire reached its political and territorial zenith during the reign of Trajan.

words.translation: Diversificarse hacia nuevas áreas de actividad

words.translation: Continuar adelante a pesar de las dificultades

native_idioms.translation: La gota que colmó el vaso

native_idioms.translation: En las buenas y en las malas

native_idioms.word: Your guess is as good as mine
native_idioms.translation: Sé tanto como tú o no tengo la menor idea

business_tech.translation: Metodología ágil de desarrollo iterativo
business_tech.example: Agile methodology divides large software roadmaps into two-week development sprints.

business_tech.example: An API gateway routes external client requests to internal private microservice endpoints.

business_tech.translation: Servidor, lógica y base de datos de una aplicación
business_tech.example: The backend is engineered in Node.js and talks directly to a PostgreSQL database.

business_tech.translation: Ancho de banda o capacidad de tiempo disponible
business_tech.example: Our engineering team lacks the bandwidth to take on a secondary codebase refactor.

business_tech.translation: Límite máximo de consumo de ancho de banda
business_tech.example: Mobile data plans often enforce a bandwidth cap on ultra-high-definition streaming.

business_tech.translation: Punto de referencia o estándar de rendimiento
business_tech.example: Our new database indexing engine sets a formidable industry benchmark.

business_tech.translation: Grandes volúmenes de datos complejos y masivos
business_tech.example: Analyzing big data helps meteorologists improve long-range hurricane path forecasting.

business_tech.translation: Cadena de bloques descentralizada
business_tech.example: Supply chain firms use private blockchain ledgers to trace pharmaceutical origins.

business_tech.translation: Cuello de botella que frena el rendimiento global
business_tech.example: Unindexed database table joins created a severe performance bottleneck during peak hours.

business_tech.translation: Computación en la nube mediante servidores remotos
business_tech.example: Cloud computing enables startups to launch global web portals without buying physical hardware.

business_tech.translation: Refactorización de código sin alterar su comportamiento
business_tech.example: Code refactoring simplified tangled callback structures into clean async/await functions.

business_tech.translation: Arranque en frío de contenedores o funciones cloud
business_tech.example: Serverless architectures optimize initialization packages to minimize cold start delays.

business_tech.translation: Cumplimiento normativo y regulatorio legal
business_tech.example: Fintech platforms must maintain strict compliance with global banking security protocols.

business_tech.translation: Concurrencia o ejecución simultánea de procesos
business_tech.example: Node.js utilizes an asynchronous event loop to handle massive network concurrency.

business_tech.translation: Contenerización de aplicaciones con Docker
business_tech.example: Containerization packages application code and dependencies into portable, isolated images.

business_tech.translation: Integración continua de código con pruebas automáticas
business_tech.example: Continuous integration runs automated linter checks and test suites on every pull request.

business_tech.translation: Multiplataforma (compatible con iOS, Android y Web)
business_tech.example: Building cross-platform apps cuts engineering and maintenance overhead significantly.

business_tech.translation: Seguridad informática contra ataques digitales
business_tech.example: Cyber security teams enforce multi-factor authentication across all remote access ports.

business_tech.translation: Integridad y coherencia de los datos almacenados
business_tech.example: Cryptographic checksums ensure data integrity during long-distance satellite transfers.

business_tech.translation: Tubería de datos para procesamiento y transformación
business_tech.example: The real-time data pipeline ingests thousands of sensor events per second into the lake.

business_tech.translation: Base de datos estructurada para almacenar registros
business_tech.example: Relational databases enforce strict data integrity through foreign keys and constraints.

business_tech.translation: Bloqueo mutuo entre procesos informáticos
business_tech.example: Careless thread synchronization can trigger a database deadlock where transactions freeze.

business_tech.translation: Aprendizaje profundo con redes neuronales multicapa
